expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "For the minutes your old pods coexist with the new schema, every request hitting those three readers on an old pod errors."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "PR A — code stops reading legacy_email... PR B — the DROP, next week, after A has been live through a full weekly traffic cycle."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "The DROP. Nothing restores it cheaply. Recovering those values means a point-in-time restore of the whole database."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "A change that reverts in two minutes is fine on a Friday. This one's recovery path is a DB restore with your team offline until Monday."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "This one's recovery path is a DB restore with your team offline until Monday."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "Want me to draft the CI check that blocks destructive DDL from landing in the same commit as application code?"

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "Merge it. Don't deploy it as one unit."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "only one of them is reversible" and "the code change... Fully reversible" vs the DROP.
